top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P002) is my first choice on voice, sustained quality and imaginative depth. As publicly described, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid, with his poetry, form one long project in which memory, the body, the city and dream are built into a distinctive metaphysical architecture, in long intricate sentences I do not find elsewhere. That is the best available evidence of maturity across an oeuvre. My confidence is moderate. I judge him through translation and public knowledge, I cannot verify his poetry and early prose, and I cannot settle whether his recurring motifs are structural development or repetition. Carson (P001) is a close second. Her voice and formal invention are real, and the round-2 narrowing of her citation to original written work answers my scope concern. The open question is whether her mid-career and later books match Autobiography of Red and Nox, and I cannot test that here. I rank Carson above no award because her case clears the bar. The support counts, including Carlberg's simulated vote, are not literary evidence and did not affect this ranking. P000 is last because both candidates have serious oeuvre-level claims.
